app_title: Didaskalos: Frequency-Based Greek Grammar Textbook Builder
subtitle: An Ancient Greek grammar textbook generated from the texts you choose — lessons ordered by what your corpus actually uses, exercises taken from it unaltered.
intro_html:
{header_image}

Didaskalos (διδάσκαλος, ‘teacher’) builds an Ancient Greek grammar textbook out of the texts you select. It reads annotated treebanks — 85 works by 25 authors and collections are built in, and you can paste your own URLs or upload XML — counts the grammatical feature of every word, and turns those counts into a syllabus. Grammar topics follow what your corpus actually uses rather than a fixed curriculum, and the exercises are authentic sentences from that corpus, each carrying its citation.

Frequency alone would make a poor teacher, so the ranking is constrained. A fixed opening — the alphabet and an orientation to nouns, adjectives and verbs — maps the system before the counts take over; lessons that depend on each other stay adjacent, so the middle voice is always followed by deponent verbs; and frequency arranges everything after that.

There are two textbook types. Case-based explains nouns and adjectives case by case — one lesson for the accusative across every declension. Declension-based first classifies every noun and adjective into declension classes (first-declension feminine, second-declension masculine, the common third-declension stem types, and so on) and orders those lessons by how frequent each class is in your own texts.

Exercises are unaltered corpus sentences, scored by word rarity and sentence length and preferring sentences whose vocabulary earlier lessons have already introduced, so difficulty climbs without any sentence being rewritten. Download the book as Markdown or HTML, and the syllabus and token tables as CSV; every book carries a colophon naming each source corpus, its license and its URL.

The lesson modules are hand-written and still under review. Being translatable is a design goal, not an afterthought: the interface and the generated textbook are available in English and Persian today, and everything language-specific lives in the lesson modules and one locale file. Translate those two and Didaskalos teaches Greek in your language — the pipeline itself does not change. If you would like to do that for your language, I would be glad to help you through it: get in touch.

input_source_help: Use the repository defaults or upload files directly.
textbook_type_help: Case-based arranges noun/adjective lessons by case (one lesson for accusative, one for genitive, ...). Declension-based first classifies every noun and adjective in the treebanks into declension classes (o-stem, a-stem, etc.) and arranges the lessons by how frequent each class is in the corpus.
custom_treebank_urls_help: One URL per line or comma-separated. These are added on top of the default treebanks loaded from didaskalos/treebanks/perseus.
upload_help: Upload one or more XML files.
no_treebanks_warning: No treebanks available. Provide treebank URLs or upload XML files.

tb_doc_title: A Frequency-Based Textbook for Ancient Greek Grammar
tb_intro_case: This syllabus organizes grammar lessons by frequency of occurrence in the selected treebanks.
tb_intro_declension: This syllabus organizes grammar lessons by frequency of occurrence in the selected treebanks, with noun and adjective lessons grouped by declension class.
tb_setting_body: This textbook is built for **{lesson_count}** lessons, drawn from **{work_count}** work(s) totalling **{token_count:,}** analyzed word tokens, organized {mode}.
tb_syllabus_mode_declension: by frequency of occurrence, with nouns and adjectives grouped by declension class
tb_corpus_custom: Custom or uploaded treebank files provided at build time.
tb_corpus_desc_perseus: The Perseus Ancient Greek Dependency Treebank (AGDT), a scholarly collection of syntactically annotated Classical Greek texts maintained by the Perseus Digital Library.
tb_corpus_desc_gorman: Vanessa Gorman's Ancient Greek Dependency Trees, a large set of annotated treebanks covering the Attic orators, historians, and other prose authors.
tb_corpus_desc_harrington: J. Matthew Harrington's treebanked commentaries, published through the Perseids platform.
tb_corpus_desc_proiel-nt: The Greek New Testament from the PROIEL treebank, a morphologically and syntactically annotated edition of the New Testament in Koine Greek.
